No, psoriasis cannot be cured with UV light therapy or any other treatment [d4][d1][d3]. According to the British Skin Foundation, "there is no cure for psoriasis," though several effective treatments are available to keep it well controlled [d4]. UV light therapy (phototherapy) works by slowing skin cell growth and decreasing inflammation, helping to minimize or significantly reduce symptoms [d1][d3]. More than 80% of patients report that phototherapy significantly improves or eliminates most symptoms, and some patients may even experience completely clear skin, but this is not the same as a cure [d3][d1][d5]. It is also important to note that overexposure to UV light can worsen symptoms and increase the risk of skin damage and skin cancer, so phototherapy should always be conducted under medical supervision [d2].
